title: The enforced CSP still allows 'unsafe-inline' scripts, so it does not stop an injected inline script if any sanitizer ever slips.

source.ref: Whole-site audit 2026-11-16 (project thread, requested by Daniel). Confidence: CONFIRMED. Audit file: audit/FINAL-BUILD-AND-REPAIR-LIST-2026-11-16.md

detail:
EVIDENCE: next.config.ts:36 script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' ... (comment at :31 says it is kept for Next's inline RSC scripts); the team already notes a nonce route at :139. I reviewed all ~60 dangerouslySetInnerHTML sinks: QR/SVG are server-generated, member rich text goes through sanitizeInlineHtml (lib/entity-blocks/block-content.ts:1031), library SVG through safeElementSvg/svg-sanitize, JSON-LD escapes '<' (components/json-ld.tsx:5). No exploitable sink found.

WHY IT MATTERS: Defence in depth only. Nonce-based CSP is a large change with checkout/Stripe interplay, so do it after launch.

FIX DIRECTION: Plan nonce-based script-src via proxy.ts after Jan 1; no action needed for launch.

2026-11-16 owner answer (Daniel, 15:01Z): move to nonce-based scripts, with a test run first and a rollback if anything breaks. This supersedes "after Jan 1" above.

2026-11-16 step 0 shipped, row stays OPEN (ADR-1954, docs/security/csp-nonce.md): the nonce-based policy is built (lib/security/csp-nonce.ts, called from proxy.ts) and is OFF. Two-step rollout, both switches blank by default and read through envFlag: (1) CSP_NONCE_REPORT_ONLY=1 sends the strict policy (nonce + 'strict-dynamic', no 'unsafe-inline' in script-src) as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only on member-app pages, beside today's enforced policy; reports reach /api/csp-report tagged policy=nonce. (2) CSP_NONCE_ENFORCE=1 enforces it on those pages, after the gate in docs/RUNBOOKS.md "Nonce-based script policy" (7 clean days, a preview check, the owner's go). Blank the switch and redeploy to roll back.

SCOPE, stated plainly: only pages under app/(main) get the nonce. Next 16 stamps a nonce only on per-request renders, and experimental SRI does not cover the inline RSC payload, so static and ISR pages (marketing, discover, help, share pages, Space websites) keep 'unsafe-inline'; removing it there would make them dynamic. This row closes when CSP_NONCE_ENFORCE is on in production. The verify probe reads the literal in next.config.ts, which stays for the static pages, so closing needs the owner's word on retiming that probe to the member-app policy.

NOT YET VERIFIED (the test run answers these): the analytics head script's hash across the proxy and page bundles; not-found pages under a member path; a real browser run with the policy on.

2026-11-18 step 1 STARTED (Daniel chose "Yes, start the test run" in the security and SEO/GEO thread, 17:59Z): CSP_NONCE_REPORT_ONLY=1 set on Vercel Production and Preview. Verified live at 18:11Z: production /events (deployment dpl_2kjsC2SkaYkaec8fqFUmz56Zv23S) sends Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only with a per-request nonce, 'strict-dynamic', 'report-sample' and the five root-script hashes, beside the unchanged enforced policy. Nothing is blocked. The seven-day gate in docs/RUNBOOKS.md "Nonce-based script policy" (section written by SEC-025) runs to 2026-11-25 at the earliest; watch runtime logs for csp.violation with policy=nonce. Row stays open until CSP_NONCE_ENFORCE is on.

verify.note: Fails on 2026-11-16 (audit run). Passes when the fix lands. Audit-written probes are direction checks; retime only with Daniel's phrase.
